name: Fugazi
label: Dischord
lede: Six albums, a five-dollar ticket, more than a thousand shows across all fifty states, and not one official T-shirt for sale.

eras.title: A word from a war book
eras.text: Minor Threat and Embrace were behind Ian MacKaye, and he wanted something slower, heavier and less shouted. The band took a year to find its shape: a bassist who'd been hauling gear, a drummer swap, and a singer who kept showing up to practice until he was in.

years.h: MacKaye finds a bass player in the crew
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] had been roadying for [[Beefeater|8c016ef4-0d18-4795-86dd-35ec90a509c9]]. He, MacKaye and [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] drummer [[Colin Sears|c9bbc03c-06bf-4c37-9f54-e95b51aede4c]] start practicing. The name comes from Mark Baker's Vietnam oral history Nam, where fugazi means false, fake, not right.
The drum stool goes to the former [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] drummer, and with him comes a Rites of Spring connection that will matter within months.

years.cap: The first-show flyer cast Picciotto as the waiter. Dischord Records archive
years.h: First show: the Wilson Center, five dollars at the door
years.p: A benefit for Dischord's State of the Union comp, on a bill with [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], Ignition and Fire Party. About 300 people pay $5. Fugazi play as a three-piece and Waiting Room is already in the set. Joey Picuri rolls a cassette, the first of hundreds.
years.xp:
The flyer drew [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] waiting on the other three, a joke that turned out to be a forecast. It was one of the rare nights Fugazi played as a trio and one of the rare nights they weren't the headliner.

The door price stuck. Five dollars became the band's target for the rest of its life, worked out on an early tour as the lowest price that could still pay for the trip.

years.p: Picciotto is singing with them by the second show. Once [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]] winds down, MacKaye asks him to join for good.

eras.title: Seven songs and a van to Europe
eras.text: Fugazi went from a D.C. rumor to a working touring band in two years. They cut their records at Don Zientara's Inner Ear in Arlington, gave music away at shows, and learned the hard way that a first album can go in the bin.

years.h: Ten shows in, a demo they hand out for free
years.p: Eleven songs at Inner Ear. Ten of them go onto cassettes given away at gigs. The full session sits in a drawer until 2014.

Recorded in June with [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]]. MacKaye plays every guitar note; Picciotto only sings. The cover photo was shot at Maxwell's in Hoboken on June 30. The drop into silence 22 seconds into Waiting Room becomes the band's calling card.

years.h: A grinding European tour, then a scrapped album
years.p: They come home and go straight into the studio to make a debut LP. Nobody likes the result.
What survived the failed album sessions, trimmed to six songs.

years.h: Recording around a chef's class schedule
years.p: Repeater gets made at Inner Ear, but Niceley is in culinary school, so the band can only work with him from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

years.h: 13 Songs: both EPs on one disc
years.p: Dischord No. 36 pairs 7 Songs with Margin Walker. For a lot of listeners, this is where Fugazi starts.

eras.title: Everyone wants in. Nobody gets in.
eras.text: Two guitars now, a punishing road schedule, and a crowd that outgrew every room. The bigger Fugazi got, the more the industry circled, and the more the band's rules (all ages, cheap tickets, Dischord only) became the story.

years.p: The first full album, and the first with Picciotto on guitar, a trebly Rickenbacker cutting against MacKaye. Jim Saah shot the cover photo. Between March 1990 and June 1991 they play around 250 shows.

years.h: Playing to the White House lawn
years.p: Days before Desert Storm, Fugazi set up in Lafayette Park for a free Gulf War protest show that also backed D.C.'s homeless. Rain, sleet and cold, and a crowd anyway. The set later turns up in Instrument.
years.xp:
It was part of a wider punk percussion protest against the coming war. Fugazi played directly in front of the White House.

Joey Picuri taped it, like almost everything else. It's in the Live Series today, sleet and all.

years.p: Niceley has become a chef and turns the job down, so the band produces itself for the first time, with Zientara engineering. It lands about two months before Nevermind changes the weather.

years.h: Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], and back home within a month
years.p: The band cuts the whole next album with Albini, hears the rough mixes and shelves it, with his blessing. They redo it at Inner Ear with Zientara and Niceley. The Chicago tapes stay in the vault for 33 years.

years.h: In on the Kill Taker · Dischord No. 70
years.p: Their first record to reach the Billboard 200, peaking at No. 153, on a label that ran out of a house in Arlington.

years.src: Wikipedia (citing Our Band Could Be Your Life) · Dischord
years.p: With alternative rock at full boil, the offers got serious. Fugazi said no to all of them.
years.xp:
The account told since is that Atlantic's Ahmet Ertegun offered them virtually anything they wanted, their own imprint and a figure north of $10 million. Fugazi turned it down. Lollapalooza wanted them to headline its 1993 tour; they thought about it and passed.

The $5 door and the all-ages rule weren't a pose. The band managed itself and kept its records on Dischord, which meant no one else got a say in what a ticket or an album cost.

eras.title: Slower, stranger, and on film
eras.text: Instead of chasing the sound that got them there, Fugazi started taking it apart in the studio: clarinet, samples, a boombox, two drum kits. At the same time, an old friend with a Super 8 camera was assembling ten years of them into a film.

years.p: Self-produced at Inner Ear and a house in Guilford, Connecticut. It opens on a boombox recording and pulls the production back from the Kill Taker punch. The tour runs 172 dates from March 1995 to November 1996.

Seven months at Inner Ear with electronic drums, synths and Canty stacking two kits over a drum machine. Fans read the title as a goodbye. It was an inside joke about the drum hits after the last track.

years.h: The roadie becomes the second drummer
years.p: To play the layered End Hits drums live, they bring in former roadie [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]] on a second kit.

years.h: Instrument: ten years on Super 8, 16mm and video
years.p: Jem Cohen, who met MacKaye in high school, cuts footage from 1987 to 1998 into a film that plays more like a diary than a rock doc. The Instrument Soundtrack (Dischord No. 120) comes out alongside it, mostly instrumentals and unreleased demos.

eras.title: The best album, then the door
eras.text: Fugazi made what a lot of fans rank as their best record almost fifteen years in, then barely toured it. Families and other lives were pulling at them, and the last run of shows ended in London without anyone announcing it as the end.

years.p: Recorded January to April at Inner Ear and Dischord House. For the first time they bring in outside players: Busher on percussion, backing vocals from Kathi Wilcox of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] and Bridget Cross of [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]], cello from Amy Domingues. Furniture + 2 arrives alongside it.
For a band that once played 250 in fifteen months, the pace drops to a crawl as the members make room for families and other projects.

years.h: Three sold-out nights at the London Forum. Then nothing.
years.p: Buff Medways and Winnebago Deal open the last night, November 4. The set runs through two encores and ends on Glueman. Nobody billed it as the final show. It was.
years.xp:
The band never announced a split. Dischord's own line is an indefinite hiatus, dated 2003, and the members have said since that they aren't broken up.

Nick Pellicciotto recorded the last night. In May 2025 it was one of the first two full shows Fugazi put on streaming services, paired with the Wilson Center tape from 1987.

eras.title: Not broken up, just not playing
eras.text: No reunion tour, no festival payday. Instead Fugazi opened the vault: nearly every show they ever played, priced the way their tickets were. Meanwhile the four of them kept making music in other bands, sometimes with each other.

q: It doesn't really become a song until it goes into someone else's ears
years.h: The Live Series: every tape, five dollars suggested
years.p: Dischord launches an archive of Fugazi shows with a sliding scale from $1 to $100. MacKaye identified unlabeled tapes by things like the accents in the crowd.
years.xp:
Joey Picuri and others had taped the band from the very first show, and MacKaye admitted the band had barely listened to them. The site grew to document more than a thousand shows with close to 900 recordings.

The same year, MacKaye said the band had turned down enormous reunion offers. Bassist Joe Lally was living in Rome by then.

q: It's not going to be money that brings us back together
years.p: Asked about reunion offers, MacKaye is blunt: they've been offered a lot, and that isn't what would bring them back.
years.xp: He said the only reason to play again would be wanting to, and the schedules lining up across two continents. That position hasn't moved.

years.p: The January 1988 giveaway tape, finally out properly, plus Turn Off Your Guns, which never made the original cassette.
An instrumental trio with guitarist Anthony Pirog. The Fugazi rhythm section, back in a room together.
MacKaye's duo partner from [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]] plus his old bass player. The debut, set for March, gets pushed to June as the pandemic shuts independent record stores.
The Live Series starts landing on Bandcamp and streaming services, beginning with the first show and the last one.

The fall 1992 recordings with Steve Albini, 33 years in the vault, released as a name-your-price Bandcamp download. Proceeds go to Letters Charity, a cause that was part of Albini's life before his death in 2024.
